nodes.prompt:
You are in an isolated git worktree of the repo {{ inputs.repo }},
on a fresh branch. Implement this task, keeping the diff focused and
touching ONLY the files this task owns (another lane edits other files
in parallel — do not stray into its territory):
  {{ inputs.task_a }}
Add or update tests. Choose a commit granularity that fits the work —
one commit per refactoring unit for refactors, per file for sweeps, per
feature slice for new code — and state your choice in the first commit
message. Commit as you go, staging only the files you changed, by
explicit path (`git add <path> ...`) — never `git add -A`, `git add .`,
or `git add -u`. End every commit message with the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>` (the attribution
convention in CONTRIBUTING.md).
Reply with a one-line summary of what you changed.

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and run the project's full checks (build + test + lint). If the diff
touches concurrency-sensitive code, ALSO stress the affected tests
(`go test <pkgs> -race -count=300`, or your stack's equivalent) —
rule 4 in this graph's header.
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background. Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. Report exactly PASS if everything succeeds, or FAIL
with the failing step.

Review this worktree's diff vs its base for style, naming, and simplicity.
Judge correctness as well, and scope: the diff must serve only this
lane's task — flag anything that strays into files another lane
could own. The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e-a | inline }}
If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.
Reply with a short bulleted list, or "no style issues found".

Push this worktree's branch and open a DRAFT pull request with
`gh pr create --draft`. Put the review in the PR body:
  {{ artifacts.review-a | inline }}
Reply with the PR URL.

You are in an isolated git worktree of the repo {{ inputs.repo }},
on a fresh branch. Do this documentation task, touching ONLY the files
this task owns (another lane edits code in parallel — do not stray
into its territory):
  {{ inputs.task_b }}
Choose a commit granularity that fits the work — per file for sweeps,
per doc section for larger rewrites — and state your choice in the
first commit message. Commit as you go, staging only the files you
changed, by explicit path (`git add <path> ...`) — never `git add -A`,
`git add .`, or `git add -u`. End every commit message with the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>` (the attribution
convention in CONTRIBUTING.md).
Reply with a one-line summary of what you changed.

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and check the docs changes: every renamed or moved reference resolves,
examples still match the code they cite, and the project's checks
still pass — docs edits can break embedded snippets and lint gates
too.
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background. Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. Report exactly PASS if everything succeeds, or FAIL
with the failing step.

Review this worktree's diff vs its base for style, naming, and simplicity.
Judge accuracy against the code it documents, tone consistency, and
scope: docs files only — flag anything that strays into code another
lane could own. The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e-b | inline }}
If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.
Reply with a short bulleted list, or "no style issues found".

Push this worktree's branch and open a DRAFT pull request with
`gh pr create --draft`. Put the review in the PR body:
  {{ artifacts.review-b | inline }}
Reply with the PR URL.
